actual_object.title: The nondegenerate root-of-unity level-one Hecke regime
actual_object.statement:
**Parameters.** Let $F$ be a field and $\xi\in F^\times$ with finite quantum characteristic $e=e(F,\xi)\in\{2,3,\dots\}$ ([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]). We work in the NONDEGENERATE branch $\xi\ne1$; then $\xi$ is a primitive $e$-th root of unity in $F$, and all statements on this page live in one of the two sub-branches: (C0) $\operatorname{char}F=0$, or (CP) $\operatorname{char}F=p>0$ with $p\nmid e$. The Hecke parameter is written $\xi$ here; it is the letter $q$ of [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]].

**Hecke side.** Fix the level-one fundamental weight $\Lambda_0$ of the cyclic affine type-$A$ datum with all $d_i=1$ and charge $0$ ([[def-cyclic-affine-type-a-cartan-datum]]). With the conventions of [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]], $H^\Lambda_d=H_{F,\xi}(S_d)$ is the finite type-$A$ Hecke algebra $T_r^2=(\xi-1)T_r+\xi$ ([[prop-cyclotomic-hecke-algebras-of-level-one-are-finite-hecke-algebras]]), and $H^\Lambda_\alpha=e_\alpha H^\Lambda_d$ are its residue-content blocks ([[def-residue-sequence-idempotents-and-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks]]).

**KLR side.** Use the type-$A$ specialization $Q^A$ of [[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]] with the same $e$ and the STANDARD homogeneous first-strand cyclotomic quotient $R^\Lambda_\alpha$ of [[def-cyclotomic-klr-quotient-at-a-dominant-weight]]: the cyclotomic relation is $y_1^{\delta_{i_1,0}}e(i)=0$, induction appends on the right, and the grading is $\deg e(i)=0$, $\deg y_r=2$, $\deg\psi_re(i)=-a_{i_ri_{r+1}}$ ([[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]). The transported grading on $H^\Lambda_\alpha$ uses a FIXED admissible local normalising series ([[cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading]]); a different series gives a graded-isomorphic transported algebra via $\rho'\rho^{-1}$, and the graded multiplicities studied below do not depend on the choice.

**Grading and Fock variables.** All grading shifts and all global-basis polynomials are in the variable $q$, $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$. Thus $\xi\in F^\times$ (the Hecke parameter, equal to the source's $\xi$) and $q$ (the grading variable, equal to the source's quantum variable) are INDEPENDENT data; the design's phrase "Ariki's normalization $\xi=q^2$" is retained only as the source dictionary of [Ariki 1996], whose Hecke parameters are powers of a square $q_{\rm src}^2$, and no numerical relation or specialization between $\xi$ and $q$ is imposed.

**Fock side.** Use the level-one symmetric model $\mathcal F_{\rm sym}$ of [[def-symmetric-group-level-one-residue-and-partition-label-convention]]: charge $0$, node residues $c-r$, standard vectors $M_\mu$ for ALL partitions $\mu$, basic/restricted labels the $e$-restricted partitions $RP_\alpha=\{\lambda:\lambda_a-\lambda_{a+1}<e,\ \operatorname{cont}(\lambda)=\alpha\}$, empty component $B(\Lambda_0)$. For $\lambda\in RP$ the conjugate $\lambda'$ is $e$-regular. Write $P(\nu)$ for the independently constructed ordinary Dipper–James Specht module and $D_{\rm DJ}^{\nu}$ for its form quotient in [[thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell]]. Define $\theta(T_r)=(\xi-1)-T_r=-\xi T_r^{-1}$, the involutive sign automorphism of [[lem-dj-bridge-sign-automorphism-and-star-dual]]. After converting right modules to left modules through the star anti-involution, the intrinsic restricted Murphy simple with label $\lambda$ is $\theta$-pullback of $D_{\rm DJ}^{\lambda'}$, not the untwisted ordinary module. This is an ungraded convention dictionary. The pullback can move blocks: on the multiplicative Jucys–Murphy elements $\theta(X_j)=X_j^{-1}$, so charge-zero residue content is sent from $\alpha$ to $-\alpha$. Thus the ordinary module before pullback has the conjugate content; no claim identifies it untwisted inside the same block. At $\xi=1$ the separate specialization theorem [[cor-dj-bridge-specialization-and-composition-multiplicity-dictionary]] identifies $\theta$ with sign tensoring over every field; $\xi=1$ remains outside the present nondegenerate regime.

No choice principle is used.
actual_object.strategy: Direct convention check. At level one $(\Lambda_0,\alpha_i)=\delta_{i,0}$, so the cyclotomic polynomial of [[def-affine-and-cyclotomic-type-a-hecke-algebras]] is $\prod_i(X_1-\xi^i)^{(\Lambda_0,\alpha_i)}=X_1-1$ and the KLR cyclotomic relation is $y_1^{\delta_{i_1,0}}e(i)=0$; the finite-characteristic hypothesis $e\in\{2,3,\dots\}$ makes $\xi\ne1$ a primitive $e$-th root, and in sub-branch (CP) the hypothesis $p\nmid e$ is exactly what makes a primitive $e$-th root exist in $F$. The type-$A$ datum and the grading are batch-24 clauses; the transport statement is the graded block isomorphism of [[thm-brundan-kleshchev-blockwise-hecke-klr-isomorphism]] with [[cor-cyclotomic-hecke-blocks-inherit-a-nontrivial-z-grading]]. The Fock-side residues, the restricted labels and the empty component are batch-9/batch-23 clauses. The ordinary dictionary uses the actual universal module-and-form comparison [[thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell]], not a rename of a cellular module. Its Laurent-unit form factor preserves radicals, including zero quotients, and gives $D_{\rm DJ}^{\lambda'}\cong(D_{\rm M}^{\lambda})^{\theta}$; apply the involution again. Right-to-left conversion sends $h\cdot m=m h^*$, and commutation $\theta *=*\theta$ preserves the same pullback dictionary. On the finite level-one tower $X_j=\xi^{1-j}T_{j-1}\cdots T_1^2\cdots T_{j-1}$. Applying $\theta(T_r)=-\xi T_r^{-1}$ to this palindrome gives $\theta(X_j)=X_j^{-1}$: the $2j-2$ signs cancel and the scalar is $\xi^{j-1}$. Generalized eigenvalues $\xi^i$ therefore become $\xi^{-i}$, proving the content reflection. No raw Hecke automorphism is claimed to preserve a fixed transported grading. The $\xi=1$ specialization is the separate arbitrary-field polytabloid specialization corollary, not an inference from a prime-field-only statement. The parameter dictionary is the naming clause of [BK 2009 §1 and §4.2] and [Ariki 1996 §1]; it makes no substitution. No choice is used.

actual_used_supplier_statements.statement:
For every commutative $R$ and $q\in R^\times$:

1. $\theta(T_i):=(q-1)-T_i=-qT_i^{-1}$ extends uniquely to an involutive $R$-algebra automorphism $\theta$ of $H=H_{R,q}(S_n)$, with $\theta(T_w)=(-q)^{\ell(w)}T_{w^{-1}}^{-1}$; $\theta$ commutes with the star anti-involution $*$ and is compatible with every base change.
2. For a right $H$-module $M$, the pullback $M^\theta$ (same underlying $R$-module, action $m\cdot h:=m\theta(h)$) is a right $H$-module; $(-)^\theta$ is exact, preserves submodules, quotients, finite composition multiplicities and simplicity, and $(M^\theta)^\theta=M$.
3. The star-contragredient $M^\circ:=\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,R)$ with $(f\cdot h)(m):=f(mh^*)$ is a right $H$-module; for finite free $M$ it is finite free of the same rank, $(-)^\circ$ commutes with base change, and $(M^\theta)^\circ=(M^\circ)^\theta$.
4. For every partition $\lambda\vdash n$, if $w_0(S_\lambda)$ is the longest element of the row subgroup, then
$$\theta(x_\lambda)=q^{\ell(w_0(S_\lambda))}y_\lambda,\qquad \theta(y_\lambda)=q^{-\ell(w_0(S_\lambda))}x_\lambda.$$
In particular $\theta(x_\lambda)$ and $y_\lambda$ differ by the unit $q^{\ell(w_0(S_\lambda))}$, and this unit factor must be carried through every form comparison. At $q=1$, $\theta$ is the pullback along the sign automorphism $w\mapsto\operatorname{sgn}(w)w$ of $R[S_n]$.

No choice principle is used.

For every commutative $R$, unit $q$ and partition $\lambda$, there is a base-change compatible isomorphism
$$\Phi_\lambda:P(\lambda)\longrightarrow C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')^\theta$$
of right $H$-modules, and an explicit unit $u_\lambda(q)=q^{\ell(w_0(S_{\lambda'}))-\ell(w_\lambda)}\in A^\times$ such that
$$G_{\lambda'}^\theta(\Phi_\lambda x,\Phi_\lambda y)=u_\lambda(q)\,\beta_{P(\lambda)}(x,y)\qquad(x,y\in P(\lambda)),$$
with $G_{\lambda'}$ the Murphy form of [[lem-dj-bridge-murphy-cellular-basis-and-cell-form]] and $\theta$ the sign automorphism of [[lem-dj-bridge-sign-automorphism-and-star-dual]]. The unit $u_\lambda$ is computed in the fixed generator and form normalizations of this page; no unnamed scalar and no potentially vanishing scalar is permitted. Consequently the form radicals and their quotients correspond after every field specialization: $D^{\lambda}_{\mathrm{DJ}}\cong(D^{\lambda'}_{\mathrm M})^\theta$, including the zero-quotient case. Over a PID with a chosen prime, the unit-scaled form identity preserves all Jantzen divisibility submodules and reductions. One also obtains $P(\lambda')\cong P(\lambda)^{\circ,\theta}$ with the exact position of the dual and $\theta$, separating same-shape duality from conjugate-sign transport. No choice principle is used.

Assume the isomorphism and unit identity of [[thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell]]. For every field $F$ at $q=1$, $P(\lambda)$ specializes to the ordinary integral-polytabloid Specht module $F\otimes_{\mathbb Z}S^\lambda_{\mathbb Z}$ of [[def-integral-specht-lattice-and-base-change]], with its standard form, and $\theta$ becomes tensoring with the sign representation; this specialization is compatible with [[lem-conjugate-specht-sign-duality-over-fields]]. For an arbitrary unit $q$ over a field, $[P(\lambda):D^{\mu}_{\mathrm{DJ}}]=[C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda'):D^{\mu'}_{\mathrm M}]$ whenever $D^{\mu'}_{\mathrm M}\ne0$, and the simultaneous sign-automorphism pullback is the same $\theta$ on both sides. For a Schur corner already proved to send the Weyl module $W(\lambda)$ to $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$ and its head $L(\lambda)$ to $D^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$, the ordinary dictionary is $F(W(\lambda'))\cong P(\lambda)^\theta$ and $F(L(\lambda'))\cong(D^{\lambda}_{\mathrm{DJ}})^\theta$, including zero; it is never the untwisted conjugate-dual identity. No Schur-algebra or source-20 convention result is a prerequisite of this conditional dictionary. No choice principle is used.

actual_object.title: The graded Specht module by homogeneous standard tableaux
actual_object.statement:
Work in the regime of [[def-nondegenerate-root-of-unity-level-one-hecke-regime]]. Fix a partition $\mu$, put $d=|\mu|$, $\alpha=\operatorname{cont}(\mu)$, and let $K(\mu)$ be the $F$-span of the Murphy elements $m_{S,T}$ of [[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]] with $S,T$ standard tableaux of a multipartition strictly dominating $\mu$; by [[thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular]] $K(\mu)$ is a two-sided ideal of $H^\Lambda_d$ and $z_\mu:=m_{t^\mu t^\mu}+K(\mu)$ is defined. Define the (level-one) **cell/Specht module** $$S(\mu):=H^\Lambda_d\,z_\mu\subseteq H^\Lambda_d/K(\mu),$$ a LEFT $H^\Lambda_d$-module lying in the block $H^\Lambda_\alpha$.

For every standard $\mu$-tableau $T$ fix a reduced decomposition $w_T=s_{r_1}\cdots s_{r_m}$ of the associated permutation and put $z_T:=T_{w_T}z_\mu$, $v_T:=\psi_{w_T}z_\mu$ in the Khovanov-Lauda presentation of [[def-type-a-cyclotomic-specialization-of-the-qg-klr-algebras]]. For a removable $i$-node $A$ of a partition $\lambda$ define $d_A(\lambda):=\#\{\text{addable }i\text{-nodes strictly below }A\}-\#\{\text{removable }i\text{-nodes strictly below }A\}$ (equivalently in the level-one symmetric residue convention of the regime) and define the **degree** of a standard tableau inductively by $\deg(\varnothing):=0$ and, for $d>0$, $\deg(T):=\deg(T_{\le d-1})+d_A(\mu)$ where $A$ is the node of $T$ containing $d$.

The definition asserts, and proves below in [[thm-graded-specht-module-has-homogeneous-tableau-basis]], that $\{v_T:T\in\operatorname{Std}(\mu)\}$ is a homogeneous $F$-basis of $S(\mu)$ making it a graded $R^\Lambda_\alpha$-module whose $q$-character is $\operatorname{ch}_qS(\mu)=\sum_T q^{\deg T}i_T$; forgetting the grading recovers the ungraded cell module. **Convention.** This is the LEFT Murphy cell module, obtained from the right cellular datum by $h\cdot m=m h^*$. Forgetting its grading, [[thm-dj-bridge-murphy-cell-is-the-same-shape-specht-dual]] identifies it with the star-contragredient dual of the same-shape independently defined ordinary Dipper–James Specht module $P(\mu)$. Separately, [[thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell]] gives $S(\mu)\cong P(\mu')^{\theta}$ after the same left-module conversion. These are two proved module comparisons, not the identification of an untwisted conjugate module. The sign pullback may change ordinary residue content from $-\alpha$ to $\alpha$; these ungraded comparisons do not assert homogeneity of the ordinary form or of a raw Hecke sign automorphism in the fixed transported grading. The labelling of simples by $e$-restricted or $e$-regular partitions is NOT asserted here; it is determined by the head-classification theorem later on this page.

No choice is used in the definition.
actual_object.strategy: This is a definition with its construction; the asserted basis, homogeneity and module structure are discharged by [[thm-graded-specht-module-has-homogeneous-tableau-basis]], and the ideal/cellular facts by [[thm-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-basis-is-cellular]]. The degree recursion is the source's (4.33); the vectors $v_T$ depend a priori on the chosen reduced decompositions, and the theorem proves the resulting grading is well defined. The same-shape ordinary duality is established by the perfect star-balanced cross-pairing of [[thm-dj-bridge-murphy-cell-is-the-same-shape-specht-dual]], which does not require a nondegenerate self-form. The separate conjugate comparison is the explicit universal signed isomorphism of [[thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell]]. Convert both right modules through star; because theta commutes with star, finite duality and sign pullback keep their stated positions. No unsupported historical source20 convention is used. No choice. Use the LEFT-handed Murphy basis: if the supplied cellular datum is right-handed, apply its anti-involution to every basis identity. Then H z_mu is a left cyclic cell module, z_T=T_w z_mu and v_T=psi_w z_mu are left actions, consistent with the left KLR modules and right-append corner functors used throughout. No identification of a right module with a left module without this conversion is made.

actual_used_supplier_statements.statement:
For every commutative $R$ and $q\in R^\times$:

1. $\theta(T_i):=(q-1)-T_i=-qT_i^{-1}$ extends uniquely to an involutive $R$-algebra automorphism $\theta$ of $H=H_{R,q}(S_n)$, with $\theta(T_w)=(-q)^{\ell(w)}T_{w^{-1}}^{-1}$; $\theta$ commutes with the star anti-involution $*$ and is compatible with every base change.
2. For a right $H$-module $M$, the pullback $M^\theta$ (same underlying $R$-module, action $m\cdot h:=m\theta(h)$) is a right $H$-module; $(-)^\theta$ is exact, preserves submodules, quotients, finite composition multiplicities and simplicity, and $(M^\theta)^\theta=M$.
3. The star-contragredient $M^\circ:=\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,R)$ with $(f\cdot h)(m):=f(mh^*)$ is a right $H$-module; for finite free $M$ it is finite free of the same rank, $(-)^\circ$ commutes with base change, and $(M^\theta)^\circ=(M^\circ)^\theta$.
4. For every partition $\lambda\vdash n$, if $w_0(S_\lambda)$ is the longest element of the row subgroup, then
$$\theta(x_\lambda)=q^{\ell(w_0(S_\lambda))}y_\lambda,\qquad \theta(y_\lambda)=q^{-\ell(w_0(S_\lambda))}x_\lambda.$$
In particular $\theta(x_\lambda)$ and $y_\lambda$ differ by the unit $q^{\ell(w_0(S_\lambda))}$, and this unit factor must be carried through every form comparison. At $q=1$, $\theta$ is the pullback along the sign automorphism $w\mapsto\operatorname{sgn}(w)w$ of $R[S_n]$.

No choice principle is used.

For every commutative $R$, unit $q$ and partition $\lambda$, there is a base-change compatible isomorphism
$$\Phi_\lambda:P(\lambda)\longrightarrow C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda')^\theta$$
of right $H$-modules, and an explicit unit $u_\lambda(q)=q^{\ell(w_0(S_{\lambda'}))-\ell(w_\lambda)}\in A^\times$ such that
$$G_{\lambda'}^\theta(\Phi_\lambda x,\Phi_\lambda y)=u_\lambda(q)\,\beta_{P(\lambda)}(x,y)\qquad(x,y\in P(\lambda)),$$
with $G_{\lambda'}$ the Murphy form of [[lem-dj-bridge-murphy-cellular-basis-and-cell-form]] and $\theta$ the sign automorphism of [[lem-dj-bridge-sign-automorphism-and-star-dual]]. The unit $u_\lambda$ is computed in the fixed generator and form normalizations of this page; no unnamed scalar and no potentially vanishing scalar is permitted. Consequently the form radicals and their quotients correspond after every field specialization: $D^{\lambda}_{\mathrm{DJ}}\cong(D^{\lambda'}_{\mathrm M})^\theta$, including the zero-quotient case. Over a PID with a chosen prime, the unit-scaled form identity preserves all Jantzen divisibility submodules and reductions. One also obtains $P(\lambda')\cong P(\lambda)^{\circ,\theta}$ with the exact position of the dual and $\theta$, separating same-shape duality from conjugate-sign transport. No choice principle is used.

Assume the isomorphism and unit identity of [[thm-dj-bridge-ordinary-specht-is-the-signed-conjugate-murphy-cell]]. For every field $F$ at $q=1$, $P(\lambda)$ specializes to the ordinary integral-polytabloid Specht module $F\otimes_{\mathbb Z}S^\lambda_{\mathbb Z}$ of [[def-integral-specht-lattice-and-base-change]], with its standard form, and $\theta$ becomes tensoring with the sign representation; this specialization is compatible with [[lem-conjugate-specht-sign-duality-over-fields]]. For an arbitrary unit $q$ over a field, $[P(\lambda):D^{\mu}_{\mathrm{DJ}}]=[C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda'):D^{\mu'}_{\mathrm M}]$ whenever $D^{\mu'}_{\mathrm M}\ne0$, and the simultaneous sign-automorphism pullback is the same $\theta$ on both sides. For a Schur corner already proved to send the Weyl module $W(\lambda)$ to $C_{\mathrm M}(\lambda)$ and its head $L(\lambda)$ to $D^{\lambda}_{\mathrm M}$, the ordinary dictionary is $F(W(\lambda'))\cong P(\lambda)^\theta$ and $F(L(\lambda'))\cong(D^{\lambda}_{\mathrm{DJ}})^\theta$, including zero; it is never the untwisted conjugate-dual identity. No Schur-algebra or source-20 convention result is a prerequisite of this conditional dictionary. No choice principle is used.
